source.title: The Grokked Illusion: True Equilibrium Mitigates Catastrophic Forgetting
source.authors: Xiaotian Zhang; Lai-Shun Chan; Yue Shang; Entao Yang; Ge Zhang

page_placements.theme: Continual random-data learning depends on plasticity and forgetting

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Tests fitting randomly generated inputs in a modified modular-arithmetic setup; the architecture is expanded before fine-tuning, so the result qualifies the scope of V3 rather than reproducing its stated setting.
record.gate_note: The study reports training accuracy after memorizing newly injected data. Only the random-noise condition bears on V3; the structured-data conditions do not measure the versions listed. The random-label claim in the Introduction is cited prior work, not a result of this study.
record.test_reason: The study uses memorization of injected synthetic data to measure catastrophic forgetting. It does not test completely random relabeling of a fixed training set or any of V3's specified input transformations. Vocabulary expansion and changed fine-tuning hyperparameters also prevent this from testing the unchanged-network recipe.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: WLMD-equilibrium models retain original-task performance better after injected-data memorization, and this advantage is associated with higher effective rank in attention and MLP layers. The authors explicitly acknowledge that the causal relationship remains unestablished.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses modular arithmetic and injects new synthetic data after training; it expands the vocabulary and fine-tunes the models, rather than randomly relabeling a fixed image training set.
record.method_sensitivity: Injected-data structure changes the amount of forgetting: the reported gap narrows as the new task becomes more structurally similar to the original.

fits_no_version.finding: Both model types exceed 99.8% combined training accuracy after vocabulary expansion and fine-tuning on original data plus 500 randomly generated samples.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pretrained modular-arithmetic transformers can accommodate additional discrete random data after expanding their vocabulary and changing the training recipe.

fits_no_version.finding: After random-data injection, original-task test accuracy falls from 100% to approximately 75% for AdamW-goldilocks and approximately 95% for WLMD-equilibrium, despite continued perfect original-task training accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Equally generalizing modular-arithmetic models can differ substantially in resistance to catastrophic forgetting during subsequent data memorization.

record.code_released: All code and models will be made publicly available upon publication; URL not stated.
record.problems: The study uses a controlled synthetic modular-arithmetic task and an expanded vocabulary; the authors state that extension to more complex tasks and architectures remains future work.
record.rows_left_out: No other reported results were retained: the structured injected-data conditions do not measure the claim versions, and the SVD and parameter-cosine measurements concern robustness mechanisms rather than the listed behaviors.

untested.parts: Completely random relabeling of the training set, chance test performance, and fitting without architecture or training-hyperparameter changes.
Relative training time for true versus random labels and convergence as the corrupted-label fraction increases.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs with the same networks.
Perfect training fit and progressively worsening test error across a sweep of random-label corruption fractions.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Preferential learning of shared real-data patterns before noise when both are available during training. Introducing noise after original-task training does not establish this preference.

record.verdict_notes: The vocabulary change and untested image conditions do not demonstrate a failure or qualification of V3; they establish that this experiment addresses a different setting. The record's V3 limits_scope verdict should therefore be removed.

versions.untested_parts: Does not randomly relabel the original training set or report its test error.
Does not compare time to fit true labels with time to fit random labels, or sweep the fraction of corrupted labels.
Does not test shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise images; random inputs are synthetic modular-task inputs, and the model vocabulary is expanded before fine-tuning.
Does not vary the fraction of randomly corrupted labels or track test error as that fraction rises.
Does not compare weight decay, dropout, or data augmentation when fitting random labels or true labels.
Does not measure whether real-label patterns are learned before random-label patterns.

rows.subject: AdamW-goldilocks NN
rows.operation_detail: Fine-tuned the vocabulary-expanded model on original training data mixed with 500 randomly generated input samples labeled with new token indices.
rows.measure: Training accuracy on the combined dataset after memorizing injected random-noise data
rows.note: The authors report both model types reach this threshold. The input data are synthetic modular-task inputs, and the vocabulary dimension was expanded before fine-tuning.
rows.check: The reported >99.8% accuracy is on the combined dataset, not specifically the injected samples. This is a valid auxiliary training result, but discrete random inputs in an expanded-vocabulary modular task do not measure V3's shuffled-pixel or Gaussian-input conditions. The approximately 215,000 parameters describe the model before vocabulary expansion.

relation.reason: Memorization supplies the interference used to study catastrophic forgetting; the study does not test completely random relabeling of a fixed training set or V3's specified input transformations.

tranche.reason: Uses noisy-data memorization to measure retention of previously learned knowledge. Vocabulary-expanded modular-task inputs and changed fine-tuning settings do not test the specified claim versions.

source_check.notes: The >99.8% threshold is explicitly reported for the combined dataset, not the injected subset alone. The authors' retention and effective-rank conclusion is accurately paraphrased; causality remains unestablished.
